title: Self-similar vector solitons for the coupled higher-order nonlinear Schrodinger equations in inhomogeneous optical fibers
abstract: We prove the existence of two kinds of self-similar vector solitons in an inhomogeneous optical fiber medium, where light propagation is governed by a pair of coupled higher-order nonlinear Schrodinger equations with varying second- and third-order dispersions, self- and cross-phase modulation non linearities, self-steepening, and linear gain/loss effects. The newly found self-similar waves comprise bright-W-shaped and kink-antikink waveforms with nonvanishing amplitudes. As a practical exam ple, we discuss the propagation dynamics of these soliton structures in a periodically distributed fiber system as well as an exponential dispersion-decreasing fiber. The results demonstrate that the parameter functions of gain/loss and third-order dispersion serve as a key factor in determining the nonlinear dynamics of self-similar vector solitons. In particular, we find that precise control over the shape and dynamic evolution of self-similar pulses can be achieved through a proper choice of the distributed third-order dispersion parameter, while the gain/loss coefficient controls their intensity.
summary: This theoretical work analyzes the existence of self-similar vector solitons in optical fibers whose properties vary along the propagation direction. By solving the coupled higher-order nonlinear Schrödinger equations using similarity transformations, the authors demonstrate that the pulse dynamics can be precisely controlled by tuning the distributed dispersion and gain/loss parameters. This provides a powerful framework for managing light pulses in complex, real-world optical media.
main_problem: The paper aims to prove the existence and analyze the dynamics of self-similar vector solitons propagating in inhomogeneous optical fibers.
main_result: Two types of self-similar vector solitons—bright-W-shaped and kink-antikink waveforms—were found, demonstrating that pulse control can be achieved by manipulating the distributed third-order dispersion and gain/loss parameters.
method: The authors employed the similarity transformation method to reduce the variable-coefficient coupled Higher-Order Nonlinear Schrödinger equations into solvable forms, allowing for the derivation of exact analytical solutions.
model_or_system: The system models light pulse propagation in inhomogeneous optical fibers, governed by coupled higher-order nonlinear Schrödinger (HNLS) equations that incorporate varying second/third-order dispersions, self/cross-phase modulation, and gain/loss effects.
key_observables: Bright-W-shaped and kink-antikink soliton waveforms, pulse intensity profiles, and the evolution of the pulse shape and trajectory.
important_parameters: Distributed third-order dispersion parameter ($D_3(z)$) and the gain/loss coefficient, which are key factors controlling the pulse shape and intensity, respectively.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on using specific ansatz solutions and making assumptions about the functional form of the variable coefficients (e.g., periodic or exponential profiles).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the intensity evolution of the found soliton solutions, showing profiles for bright/W-shaped solitons and kink/antikink solitons under various parameter settings.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the coupled HNLS equations, applies similarity transformations to handle variable coefficients, derives general self-similar wave solutions, and then analyzes the dynamics under specific parameter variations (periodic or exponential dispersion/loss).
why_interesting: The mathematical techniques used (similarity transformations on variable-coefficient PDEs) are highly relevant to modeling complex, non-uniform physical systems encountered in quantum optics and nonlinear wave physics.
